description: Anti-authoritarian political traditions that reject coercive hierarchy and centralized domination.
accepted_subtypes: Anarcho-communism; anarcho-syndicalism; mutualism; anarcho-capitalism; libertarian socialism
analysis_guidance: Use for profiles where anti-authoritarianism and opposition to centralized power are structurally defining.

description: Movements and traditions centered on national liberation, anti-imperialism, and political emancipation from colonial rule.
accepted_subtypes: Anti-apartheid democracy; liberation nationalism; pan-Africanism; anti-imperial socialism; decolonial republicanism
analysis_guidance: Use when anti-imperial or national-liberation politics are more central than a standard left/right label.

description: Political traditions focused on Arab unity, sovereignty, anti-imperial positioning, and regional national identity.
accepted_subtypes: Baathism; Nasserism; Arab socialism; pan-Arabism
analysis_guidance: Use for Arab unity or Arab sovereignty projects, including socialist and authoritarian variants.

description: Traditions and regimes emphasizing centralized authority, coercive order, hierarchy, and limited political pluralism.
accepted_subtypes: Military authoritarianism; personalist rule; bureaucratic authoritarianism; authoritarian nationalism
analysis_guidance: Use when regime form and coercive authority are more defining than a narrower ideological family.

description: Moderate or synthesis-oriented positioning combining reformism, institutionalism, and mixed economic preferences.
accepted_subtypes: Liberal centrism; radical centrism; technocratic centrism; third way
analysis_guidance: Use for profiles whose defining feature is synthesis, institutional moderation, or avoidance of strong ideological polarity.

description: Anti-capitalist traditions centered on class struggle, collective ownership, and the abolition or transcendence of capitalism.
accepted_subtypes: Marxism; Leninism; Maoism; Stalinism; Trotskyism; council communism
aliases: communist; communism; marxism; leninism; maoism; stalinism; trotskyism
analysis_guidance: Use when collective ownership and anti-capitalism are structurally central rather than merely redistributive.

description: Traditions emphasizing continuity, social order, inherited institutions, authority, and cultural or moral stability.
accepted_subtypes: Liberal conservatism; national conservatism; traditionalism; Christian democracy; Gaullism
analysis_guidance: Use when preservation, continuity, order, or traditional institutions are defining traits.

description: Controlled taxonomy family for Critical theory.
accepted_subtypes: Critical theory
analysis_guidance: Use when Critical theory is the clearest broad family for the profile.

description: Political traditions prioritizing ecological limits, sustainability, environmental protection, and critique of unrestricted productivism.
accepted_subtypes: Green politics; eco-socialism; degrowth; conservative environmentalism; eco-liberalism
analysis_guidance: Use when ecological constraint is a primary organizing principle rather than a secondary policy area.

description: Ultra-nationalist, authoritarian, anti-liberal and anti-communist traditions often centered on hierarchy, mythic unity, and political violence.
accepted_subtypes: Fascism; Nazism; clerical fascism; neo-fascism
aliases: fascist; fascism; nazi; nazism; national socialism
analysis_guidance: Use carefully for historically or analytically fascist profiles, not as a generic insult for authoritarianism.

description: Traditions centered on gender equality, political representation, and critique of patriarchal structures.
accepted_subtypes: Liberal feminism; socialist feminism; radical feminism; intersectional feminism
analysis_guidance: Use when gender equality and feminist analysis are central to the profile's political identity.

description: Traditions emphasizing individual rights, constitutional government, pluralism, civil liberties, markets, and legal equality.
accepted_subtypes: Classical liberalism; social liberalism; neoliberalism; liberal internationalism
analysis_guidance: Use for rights-based, constitutional, pluralist, or market-oriented liberal traditions.

description: Traditions emphasizing individual autonomy, voluntary exchange, and skepticism toward state intervention.
accepted_subtypes: Right-libertarianism; left-libertarianism; objectivism; minarchism; anarcho-capitalism
analysis_guidance: Use when individual autonomy and anti-statism are stronger markers than generic liberalism or conservatism.

description: Controlled taxonomy family for Military leadership.
accepted_subtypes: Military leadership
analysis_guidance: Use when Military leadership is the clearest broad family for the profile.

description: Traditions defending hereditary monarchy, dynastic legitimacy, or monarchical constitutional order.
accepted_subtypes: Absolute monarchism; constitutional monarchism; traditional monarchism; royalism
analysis_guidance: Use for figures whose legitimacy or institutional project is explicitly monarchical.

description: Traditions emphasizing sovereignty, nationhood, collective identity, national priority, and political self-determination.
accepted_subtypes: Civic nationalism; ethnic nationalism; national populism; sovereigntism; revolutionary nationalism
analysis_guidance: Use when national sovereignty, identity, and priority are central organizing principles.

description: Controlled taxonomy family for Other.
accepted_subtypes: Other
analysis_guidance: Use when Other is the clearest broad family for the profile.

description: Controlled taxonomy family for Political realism.
accepted_subtypes: Political realism
analysis_guidance: Use when Political realism is the clearest broad family for the profile.

description: Traditions where political order, law, or legitimacy is strongly shaped by religious doctrine, institutions, or identity.
accepted_subtypes: Political Islam; Christian democracy; theocracy; religious conservatism
aliases: islamism; political islam; christian democracy; theocracy; religious politics
analysis_guidance: Use when religious doctrine or religious identity is a central basis of politics.

description: Political logic opposing a claimed people against elites, establishments, or corrupt institutions.
accepted_subtypes: Left populism; right populism; national populism; agrarian populism
analysis_guidance: Use when the people-versus-elite structure is defining, whether left, right, or syncretic.

description: Controlled taxonomy family for Progressivism.
accepted_subtypes: Progressivism
analysis_guidance: Use when Progressivism is the clearest broad family for the profile.

description: Traditions emphasizing citizenship, civic virtue, constitutional order, public liberty, and opposition to arbitrary rule.
accepted_subtypes: Civic republicanism; revolutionary republicanism; classical republicanism
analysis_guidance: Use for profiles centered on citizenship, public liberty, constitutionalism, and anti-monarchical or anti-arbitrary rule.

description: Reformist left tradition combining democracy, welfare policy, labor rights, redistribution, and regulated capitalism.
accepted_subtypes: Laborism; democratic reformism; welfare-state politics; Nordic social democracy
aliases: social democrat; social democracy; labourism; laborism
analysis_guidance: Use for democratic, reformist, welfare-oriented left politics that do not seek full abolition of capitalism.

description: Left traditions emphasizing equality, redistribution, social ownership, labor power, and collective control of economic life.
accepted_subtypes: Democratic socialism; libertarian socialism; market socialism; African socialism; guild socialism
analysis_guidance: Use for broad socialist orientations that are not specifically communist or social-democratic.

description: Traditions emphasizing expert administration, planning, technical governance, and policy rationalization.
accepted_subtypes: Technocratic centrism; developmental technocracy; expert-led planning
aliases: technocrat; technocracy; expert government; technical planning
analysis_guidance: Use when expert administration and technical governance are central to the profile.
